analysis.evidence: מִחוּט וְעַד שְׂרוֹךְ נַעַל means “from a thread to a sandal strap.” Abram names two small possessions, then extends his oath to מִכָּל אֲשֶׁר לָךְ, anything belonging to the king.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition מִ־, a form of מִן meaning “from,” introduces the masculine singular absolute noun חוּט.

draft.change: Add the noun שְׂרוֹךְ with its sandal-strap sense and correct the supplied spatial gloss for this occurrence.
draft.definition: A strap used to fasten a sandal.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:23 pairs a sandal strap with a thread. Isaiah 5:27 identifies its function by saying that no strap of the soldiers’ sandals has come loose.

analysis.evidence: In שְׂרוֹךְ נַעַל, נַעַל identifies the sandal to which the strap belongs. Abram pairs the strap with a thread as he swears to take nothing belonging to the king. Isaiah 5:27 confirms the sense by describing a sandal strap coming loose.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew common noun, masculine singular construct. The following noun נַעַל completes the phrase “the strap of a sandal.”
analysis.sense: A strap used to fasten a sandal.

analysis.evidence: In שְׂרוֹךְ נַעַל, “the strap of a sandal,” שְׂרוֹךְ names the strap and נַעַל identifies the footwear it belongs to. Abram refuses to take even a thread or a sandal strap.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
